comments.text:
One thing: There was little to no talk about the big reduction in latency you get when you use DLSS versus native resolution. Everything was centered around any possible loss of image quality versus higher frame rates. I never heard anyone talk about the feel of gameplay benefit you get by using DLSS in terms of a cost/benefit of image quality to gameplay feel. Since the image quality loss of DLSS is very small in the areas where it does look worse (it often looks better in some areas, as well), then how big of a deal could the latency reduction have been? Now frame generation comes along with a latency higher than DLSS 2 but sometimes still lower than native with no DLSS at all, and latency has become a big deal.

My personal opinion? There's a lot of paranoid sensitivity to "flaws". Test the gameplay feel in a double-blind experiment to see whether a difference between 28 ms and 38 ms is noticeable. And if it is, it still raises the question of why this issue was in general not brought up when talking about DLSS 2. I know in the past increase in smoothness and latency reduction went hand in hand, but there wasn't any big push to deliberately consider the latency when judging the merits of DLSS 2.

6:15 I bet latency will be way better in a few years just by the natural progression of neural frame generation tech.
The quality of interpolated frames is obviously great. And in a few years extrapolation could be as good as interpolation is now. instead of using frames 2 and 3 to generate frame 2.5, DLSS 4 might use frames 1 and 2 to generate frame 2.5, allowing it to start that work without waiting for frame 3, and introduce no latency at all when compared to pure upsampling. The quality will never be quite as good as interpolation because the input data is less relevant, but it only needs to be good.

Frame extrapolation could have a negative impact on latency if it generates more than one frame ahead. This must introduce overshooting the motion that would come from the user input, so maybe in 10 years nvidia will be looking into making their GPUs peek at mouse signals to help with it. The SSD is moving to the graphics card, I don't think it's unimaginable for a USB hub to follow.
